meta.about: RuneScape: Dragonwilds bestiary for Scorned Wilderness raid speedrunning. Raid enemies first in route order, then other bosses, then every other monster with a wiki infobox. Every value carries a source; anything no source states is "unknown". Nothing here is measured in-game.
sources: RuneScape: Dragonwilds Wiki (https://dragonwilds.runescape.wiki) via MediaWiki API, fetched 2026-11-03: Infobox Monster, drop tables, update history, Strategies subpages, RSDWArchive datamined loot pages
Official Steam patch notes (data/patchnotes.json) and wiki Update: mirrors

fields.stats: per power-level version: health, power level, location (wiki infobox)
fields.route: raid split index 0-4 (Dragontail Vines, Fragments of Ghornfell, The Shattered Stronghold, Cataclysm Keep, Kuldra's Sanctum) and route.js skip id
fields.unknown: fields no source states — need in-game measurement

mechanics.name: Snare (Ranged 12)
mechanics.summary: Ground trap that roots enemies that walk into it for 8 s; 45 s cooldown.

facts.text: Unlocked at level 12 Ranged; costs 15 astral + 10 nature runes.

src.quote: is a Ranged spell that is unlocked at level 12 Ranged

facts.text: Places a floating star with a circular trap; enemies that run/walk to the star are stunned for eight seconds.

src.quote: stunning all enemies that run or walk to the star at the centre for eight seconds

facts.text: Can be triggered remotely by shooting the star (ranged/magic) while monsters are in the circle; melee attacks cannot trigger it.

src.quote: Players can also activate the spell at a distance if the player launches a ranged/magic attack towards the star whilst the monsters are inside the circle.
players who place this spell cannot activate the star with melee attacks

facts.text: Venomous Trapper (Ranged 40) adds a poison cloud to the trap.

src.quote: At level 40, players unlock the Venomous Trapper which triggers a cloud of poison when it is active

facts.text: Cooldown reduced to 45 s in 1.0 (was 60 s).

src.quote: Snare's cooldown has been reduced to 45 seconds. (previously 60 seconds)

facts.text: Usable inside vaults.

src.quote: This spell may be used on land or inside vaults.

facts.text: Boss interaction: no source documents whether bosses can be snared - unknown.

src.quote: Those caught inside become rooted in place for a short time.

facts.text: Recommended for crowd control, e.g. lesser demons in Dowdun Reach.

src.quote: especially against things like the lesser demons in doubt of reach.

mechanics.name: Confuse (Magic 30)
mechanics.summary: Makes an aggressive enemy fight other monsters for 45 s; not on bosses/minibosses.

facts.text: Magic 30, 25 astral runes, 120 s cooldown.

src.quote: cooldown = 120s

facts.text: Target attacks other nearby monsters for 45 seconds or until it dies; attacking it yourself breaks the spell and it retargets you.

src.quote: causes it to attack other nearby monsters for 45 seconds, or until it dies from attacking another enemy
It is recommended not to attack the enemy under the Confuse spell, as the spell will break and the enemy will target the player.

facts.text: Cast range 40 m; only affects aggressive monsters within a 30 m radius; you get loot from monsters the confused enemy kills.

src.quote: Players can cast the Confuse spell on enemies up to 40 metres away, and it will only affect aggressive monsters within a 30-metre radius.
If the enemy under the Confuse spell kills another enemy, players can receive the deceased enemy's loot.

facts.text: Does not work on Garou thane, Dire wolf, KotHaar (need Greater Confuse), training dummy, or boss and miniboss monsters.

src.quote: Garou thane (requires the Greater Confuse perk)
KotHaar (requires the Greater Confuse perk)
Boss and miniboss monsters

facts.text: Explicitly immune: Goblin Thug, Rotsworn Reanimator, Aggressive Terrorbird.

src.quote: They are known to be immune against Confuse and Enfeeble.
immune = * Confuse

facts.text: Quest note: for Biohazard, corrupted ravens must be killed directly, not via Confuse.

src.quote: Note that players must kill these corrupted ravens directly and not use Confuse on other monsters while killing these ravens.

facts.text: Turns one of a group against the rest - cuts incoming damage as well as adding damage.

src.quote: you're reducing the amount of damage you're taking.

mechanics.name: Greater Confuse (Magic 44 perk)
mechanics.summary: Extends Confuse to stronger creatures (thanes, Garou King, dire wolves, KotHaar); still not zogres, dragons, Tok-Xil.

facts.text: Unlocked at Magic 44; lets Confuse hit Garou thane, Garou King, Dire wolf.

src.quote: allowing players to cast Confuse on more powerful enemies

facts.text: Mini-bosses such as zogres, dragons and Tok-Xils are still unaffected.

src.quote: Mini-bosses such as zogres, dragons, and Tok-Xils are not affected by this spell.

facts.text: 0.10 and 0.11 added more monsters to the Greater-Confuse-only list.

src.quote: Several more monsters were added to the list of monsters only affected by Greater Confuse.

mechanics.name: Enfeeble (Magic 61)
mechanics.summary: Weakens the target's attacks; 75 s cooldown; some 1.0 mobs are immune.

facts.text: Magic 61, 20 astral + 20 water runes, 75 s cooldown; "Weakens the attacks of the targeted opponent." Exact reduction: unknown.

src.quote: Weakens the attacks of the targeted opponent.

facts.text: Immune: Blazing Black Knight, Black Knight Crusader, Rotsworn Reanimator, Goblin Thug, Aggressive Terrorbird.

src.quote: immune = Enfeeble
immune = Enfeeble
immune = * Enfeeble

facts.text: Whether bosses are affected: no source - unknown.

src.quote: Enfeeble is a Magic spell.

mechanics.name: Parry and stagger
mechanics.summary: Last-moment block staggers most enemies (~3 s) for +25% damage; bosses like Velgar are stagger-immune.

facts.text: Parry unlocks at Attack 5: block at the last moment to stagger the attacker for roughly 3 seconds.

src.quote: parry incoming attacks to prevent damage, and stagger the attacker for roughly 3 seconds

facts.text: Bosses such as Velgar are not staggered (Stagger page lists General Velgar: Immune).

src.quote: Most enemies are staggered by different amounts, except for bosses such as Velgar.

facts.text: After a parry there is a minimum 0.550 s before you can attack.

src.quote: After a successful parry, there is a minimum delay of 0.550s

facts.text: Parrying regains some stamina.

src.quote: parrying can regain some stamina

facts.text: Enemies can be staggered by abyssal whip special, warhammer special, or parry; staggered targets take 25% more damage.

src.quote: Abyssal whip's special action will stagger non-immune enemies
the incoming damage to the attacker is dealt 25% more damage

facts.text: Enemies need 0.5 s after a stagger ends to recover; melee set bonus does not apply during that recovery.

src.quote: Enemies take 0.5s after a stagger wears off to regain consciousness and aggression.

facts.text: You get staggered by blocking with no stamina or blocking an unblockable without Tempest Shield (e.g. Garou berserker red attack, vault hulk double slam).

src.quote: Blocking while stamina is depleted.
Attempting to block an unblockable attack (without the use of Tempest Shield)

facts.text: Some boss-type enemies stagger at 50% HP, e.g. Abyssal demon.

src.quote: Some boss-type enemies will become staggered upon reaching 50% HP.

facts.text: Shielded garou (thane/King) block everything until their stance breaks (thane: 3 s stagger), then attack while stagger-immune.

src.quote: When attacked, they will block all attacks until their stance is broken, staggering them for three seconds.

facts.text: Video claim: a successful parry refunds 50% of MAX stamina and opens a visceral (cinematic punish) attack; powerful telegraphed attacks cannot be parried - dodge those.

src.quote: A successful parry gives you 50% of your maximum stamina back.
A successful parry also gives you the opportunity to perform a visceral attack.
Not every attack can be parried.

facts.text: Second source (GamerCory) agrees: successful parry restores 50% of max stamina and can open a visceral follow-up.

src.quote: A successful parry restores 50% of your maximum stamina.
you can create an opportunity to perform a visceral attack.

mechanics.name: Tempest Shield (Attack 11)
mechanics.summary: Air shield that blocks ALL damage while blocking (including unblockables); burst knockdown at end.

facts.text: Prevents all damage while blocking for a limited time; triggers a burst when it ends. 45 s cooldown (1.0).

src.quote: Conjure a Shield of Air Magic that prevents all damage while blocking for a limited time, triggering a powerful burst when the spell ends.
Tempest Shield's base cooldown has been reduced from 60 seconds to 45 seconds.

facts.text: End burst knocks nearby foes to the ground if the shield is raised.

src.quote: knocking nearby foes to the ground

facts.text: Cast before an encounter; there is rarely time once in battle.

src.quote: It is recommended to always cast it before an encounter

facts.text: Blocks "unblockable" boss attacks (e.g. Black Knight Titan Leap/overheads).

src.quote: as it blocks more variety of attacks, even unblockable ones

mechanics.name: Surge / Afterimage
mechanics.summary: Three 8 m stamina-free dodges; Afterimage decoy pulls aggro for 10 s.

facts.text: Surge (Magic 11) gives three Surge dodges for two minutes; each travels eight metres.

src.quote: Upon casting, players receive three Surge dodges
Activating a Surge charge causes the player to travel eight metres

facts.text: Afterimage (Magic 25): first Surge charge leaves a decoy for 10 s that enemies attack instead.

src.quote: leaving behind an illusory image for 10 seconds after using the first Surge charge

facts.text: Strategy pages: Surge dodges cost no stamina.

src.quote: Surge would allow you to dodge attacks at a greater distance three times, costing no stamina.

mechanics.name: Stamina, dodging, blocking
mechanics.summary: Stamina gates attacks, dodges and blocks; hydration sets regen, rest sets max.

facts.text: Dodge costs 20, jump 10, running 4/s; successful shield block 17 (holding block is free).

src.quote: Holding a block does not consume stamina.

facts.text: Regeneration starts after 3 s without stamina actions; magic 1/3 set bonus halves the delay.

src.quote: After the player takes no stamina-requiring actions for 3s, stamina regeneration will begin.

facts.text: Hydration sets regen: 0.75/s at 0 up to 6.0/s at 100 hydration; low rest caps max stamina (80/60/40).

src.quote: For every 25 points of hydration, base stamina regeneration will increase.

facts.text: Dodging can animation-cancel most player animations (e.g. cast Abyssal Snare then dodge).

src.quote: Dodging can animation cancel most player animations in the game.

facts.text: Keep enough stamina in reserve for one dodge or block.

src.quote: Never spend all your stamina. Always keep enough in reserve or one dodge or one block.

facts.text: Common dodge mistake: dodging too early; enemies wind up, attack, recover. Dodge sideways to stay in counter range.

src.quote: they dodge too early, waste stamina, and still get hit.
Sometimes dodging sideways keeps you close enough to immediately counterattack.

facts.text: Bosses: stand at their sides rather than in front, which gives them access to every attack.

src.quote: Standing directly in front of a boss usually gives them access to every attack they have.

facts.text: Use a crossbow to pull enemies one at a time.

src.quote: consider carrying a crossbow, specifically for pulling enemies one at a time.

facts.text: One magic armour piece gives -50% stamina regen delay; 2 melee + 1 magic recommended for melee.

src.quote: with just one piece of magic armor equipped, you get a 50% reduction to your stamina regeneration delay

facts.text: Since 1.0 weapon specials use a separate special-attack energy, not stamina.

src.quote: weapon special attacks now use a separate energy resource rather than consuming your regular stamina.

facts.text: Several spells (Enchant Weapon, Windstep, Surge) can be cast while moving.

src.quote: This includes spells such as Enchant Weapon, Wind Step, and Surge

facts.text: Sprint attacks (Attack 13) give a lunging opener after a short sprint.

src.quote: you can sprint towards an enemy and attack after running just a short distance.

mechanics.name: Damage types, weaknesses, hitsplats
mechanics.summary: Melee = slash/stab/crush; magic = air/fire/water (+earth); weak spots crit with no cooldown.

facts.text: Melee weapons deal slash, stab or crush; ranged one type; spells air, fire, water.

src.quote: Melee weapons have 3 damage types: slash, stab, and crush.
There are three spell damage types: air, fire, and water.

facts.text: Hitsplats show critical, resistance and weakness damage.

src.quote: which indicate when a target is receiving critical damage, is resistant to a damage type, or is weak to the damage type

facts.text: Weak spots give critical damage with no crit cooldown.

src.quote: Note that there is no cooldown for critical damage when targeting the monsters' weak spots.

facts.text: Air magic: high single-target damage and knockdown; water magic slows and heals; fire magic AoE and builds Burning.

src.quote: dealing high single target damage and knocking your enemies down
damage and slow your enemies while also healing yourself and your allies

facts.text: An immunity hitsplat means that damage type is fully negated.

src.quote: Immunity negates all damage from that damage type.

facts.text: No combat triangle: each armour type defends best vs its own style.

src.quote: each combat style's armour provides defences against its counterpart

facts.text: Opening on an unaware enemy (e.g. longbow) gives a damage bonus; wind spells knock down/stagger groups for melee follow-up; whetstone/magical focus = 15% damage for 10 minutes.

src.quote: If the enemy hasn't noticed you yet, you do get a damage bonus for that as well.
you can knock enemies down or stagger them, especially with the wind spells.
It gives you 15% damage multiplier and lasts for 10 minutes.

facts.text: Weapon names can mislead: the goblin "Swingslash" is a crush weapon; zombie axe deals both slash and crush.

src.quote: But actually, it's a crush weapon.
it gives you both slash and crush.

mechanics.name: Poison
mechanics.summary: DoT of 3 or 4 HP/s; natural recovery costs ~half your HP; antipoison/Fungal Fortitude.

facts.text: Inflicted poison deals 3 or 4 damage per second depending on source; natural recovery deals roughly half the health bar.

src.quote: Inflicted Poison will do either 3 damage/second or 4 damage/second, depending on the source.
it will deal roughly half the player's health bar during the process

facts.text: Antipoison, Antipoison II and Fungal Fortitude prevent environmental buildup and resist poison attacks.

src.quote: help prevent Poison buildup from the environment and grant some resistance to poison-based attacks

facts.text: Players can poison via weapon poison or by parrying with the dragonblight shield.

src.quote: Parrying enemy attacks with the dragonblight shield

mechanics.name: Burning
mechanics.summary: 8 HP/s for 6 s (48 total); antifire prevents; dodge-roll or water shortens.

facts.text: Burning deals 8 damage per second for 6 seconds (48 total).

src.quote: The Burning debuff applies 8 damage per second for 6 seconds (48 damage total) to the player's health.

facts.text: Avoided with antifire potions; duration reduced by dodge rolling or entering water.

src.quote: Its duration can be reduced by dodge rolling or entering water.

facts.text: Antifire perk removes Burning stacks and grants 33% resistance to buildup; 300 s (antifire) / 600 s (super).

src.quote: is a perk that removes Burning stacks and grants 33% resistance from Burning buildup

facts.text: Velgar, Imaru, Black Knight Titan, Fuzan, KotHaar and dragons are burn-immune - skip fire runes/arrows there.

src.quote: he is immune to Burning effect

mechanics.name: Bleed
mechanics.summary: Meter that bursts for 30-32 damage when full.

facts.text: Builds a meter; deals 30-32 damage instantly when full.

src.quote: It builds up a meter that will deal 30-32 damage instantly if the bar is full.

facts.text: Players apply bleed with weapon barbs / barbed arrows (Ranged 22) or abyssal whip (25 bleed build-up).

src.quote: Unlocks the recipe for weapon barbs, which can be used to imbue melee weapons with Bleed or to craft Barbed arrows.

mechanics.name: Shocked
mechanics.summary: Meter that empties your stamina when full.

facts.text: From wild lapulis vines and lightning (Stormtouched Highlands, Umbral Sands sandstorms); full meter completely drains stamina.

src.quote: It builds up a meter that, once full, will completely drain the victim's stamina.

mechanics.name: Wither / Soul Rift
mechanics.summary: Fellhollow meter; full = Soul Rift (needed to hurt Imaru's spectral form).

facts.text: Builds from withered water/ground or Rotsworn attacks; when full you enter a Soul Rift state; Steadfast Stomach slows it.

src.quote: This causes them to enter a Soul Rift state.
Consuming a food with the Steadfast Stomach perk slows down the accumulation of Wither.

facts.text: Running out of time while Soul Rifted is instant death; while rifted you cannot heal (Imaru strategy).

src.quote: Running out of time while soul rifted (instant death)

mechanics.name: Scorch (Umbral Sands)
mechanics.summary: Sunlight meter; full drains 1 HP + 1.5 hydration per second; 5 resistance sources = immune.

facts.text: Builds in direct sunlight in Umbral Sands, falls off in shade or at night; when full drains 1 health and 1.5 hydration per second.

src.quote: When the meter fills, it will drain 1 health and 1.5 hydration per second.

facts.text: Time in sun before Scorch: 0 sources 80 s, 1: 105 s, 2: 160 s, 3: 330 s, 4: 480 s, 5: full protection (desert armour, Frosted Flavours, cooling infusions, monkfish skewers, Umbral kebab stack).

src.quote: The more sources of Scorch resistance a player has, the longer they can remain in direct sunlight.

facts.text: Buildup about halved near sunrise (~7:30) and sunset (~20:00).

src.quote: build up is reduced to about half near sunrise

facts.text: Bug: with <5 sources, building scorch then swapping to 5 and stepping into shade builds instead of lowering.

src.quote: There is currently a bug where having less than 5 sources of Scorch resistance

mechanics.name: Boss / spawning rules
mechanics.summary: Generic boss behaviour and respawn rules.

facts.text: Lodestones can interfere with certain bosses spawning (Garou King).

src.quote: Lodestones can interfere with certain bosses spawning, such as the Garou King.

facts.text: Monsters respawn in 1-3 in-game days depending on type/location (many 1.0 elites list 4 days; zogres 8 days).

src.quote: Monsters can respawn between one to three days
Zogres have an 8-day respawn delay after being killed.

facts.text: Abyssal demons teleport to the player if too far away or in an area they cannot reach (anti-safespot).

src.quote: Abyssal demons will teleport to the player if the player is either too far away or in an inaccessible area to the demon.

facts.text: Ring of life teleports you to your bed at 1 HP or 10% HP (bail-out in boss fights).

src.quote: The ring of life provides a teleport back to your bed when the player's HP is reduced to 1 or 10% of the player's max health, whichever comes first.

facts.text: Lifeward/overhealth was removed in 0.12.0.

src.quote: Lifeward, healing potions, and Shield Ward perk effects have been removed from the game

src.quote: - Soulscourge skip (0:40): eat food while holding E. Start holding E BEFORE you take damage or it'll stop you.
the air anima ASAP before the soul score starts cuz if you hold E before it does starts
here I'm holding E and then I'm just eating through the damage.
So here they change it. They made the air anima a lot faster, so you actually have time to to eat.

tactics_speedrun.tip: Casual fast runs also just tank it and go straight on to the black dragon.

src.quote: Generally speaking, I would get this part and take the damage and

gear.tip: Bring Fleet Foot Infusion and food; eat to ~100 before the deliberate falls that follow.

src.quote: You don't have to eat all the way to full, but eat just like about 100.

src.quote: '''Soulscourge''' is a status effect triggered when a player's Toxicity bar is filled.
During this time, Soulscourge deals 10 damage per second (50 damage total)

src.quote: Confuse the archer, dodge the pack, run to the back of the earth anima.
stand behind the earth anima. That way if he launches any sort of attack like fire or poison, it hits the anima, it doesn't hit you, right?
1:28 Confuse archer + dodge black dragon

tactics_speedrun.tip: Just run past BD1 and out of the room.

src.quote: We just run past this dragon and get out of this room.

We're going to run right by them.

src.quote: My advice for almost every fight in this raid is kill the odds first. Don't let five enemies stack up on you while you're trying to focus the strongest enemy.
Your first major fight is against the black dragon alongside several additional enemies including the skeletons.

the scariest thing about the raid is the black dragons and also the parkour as well.
some form of an [[Anti-Dragon Shield]] or some [[Super Antifire Potion|Super Antifire Potions]]

attacks.counter: Become Soul Rifted (fill Wither) and hit her (~3 hits per SuperStooob) to cancel, or wait it out.

src.quote: She will charge up an explosive attack that can do high damage (typically around 50) and push you toward the platform edge.
after we are soul rifted, we want to attack Immaru about three times. That's going to cancel the big charge attack.

attacks.name: Circling airborne breath
attacks.pattern: Phase 3+: flies and breathes fire around the arena.
attacks.counter: Stay in the centre of the arena (or go to the outsides); use the time to eat/re-buff.

src.quote: She will fly in the air and breathe fire around the arena, stay in the centre until she stops
when she does the circling airborne breath, you can either stay right in the middle of the arena or just go to the outsides.

attacks.name: Explosive rot rocks
attacks.pattern: Late phase 3: explosive rot rocks spawn near you; they hit at some range.
attacks.tell: Rocks pop up around the arena.
attacks.counter: Keep away; can be used deliberately to get Withered faster.

src.quote: she will summon explosive rot rocks near you, be sure to avoid them
Sometimes I will actually use these as a way to get withered faster during the fight.

attacks.pattern: Rears up on two legs, jumps down sending spikes and breathes fire down on the arena.
attacks.counter: Step back and dodge the spikes (use a crossbow), or stay close attacking her tail away from the fire.

src.quote: she also does a stomping fire attack where she gets up on two legs and continues to jump down.

attacks.name: Rotsworn summons
attacks.pattern: During spectral phases she summons rotsworn thralls; a necromancer keeps spawning more.
attacks.counter: Kill the necromancer first (it spawns the rotsworn), then cleanse at a Purification Pool.

src.quote: Be aware rotsworn thralls will appear to attack you.
the necromancer is the enemy that is spawning the rotsworn enemies.

attacks.name: Landing shockwaves (multi)
attacks.pattern: On landing she sends shockwaves; later in the fight several at once (GamerCory saw about four).
attacks.tell: She lands at the edge / centre.

src.quote: she's going to send out that like shock wave. All you have to do is just double jump and get away from it.
I think she did like four at a time.

attacks.name: Double-pass fire swipe
attacks.pattern: Later she swipes fire across the platform and brings it back, so you must clear it twice.
attacks.counter: Double jump over it twice - keep stamina for both.

src.quote: she's actually going to go and do a swipe all the way across and then she's going to bring it all the way back for the fire.
So you're going to have to double jump twice over it.

as long as you're using some kind of ranged mechanic or ranged weapon, you really don't have to worry about the fire at all.
